Hi Alyssa,

Thanks for sharing the questionnaire. A few points from Redwood Security to make the exchange efficient:
1) SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II attestation for the 2025 audit period — enclosed is a SOC2-summary-202512.pdf (high level). Full report will be provided under an NDA to a named security contact.
2) Logs & retention: default diagnostic logs are retained 365 days; we can extend retention under a contract amendment.
3) Encryption & KMS: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) for Private deployments; keys are never exported.
4) Scanning cadence & method: we recommend weekly external (unauthenticated) scanning of public endpoints, monthly authenticated scans of the control plane and management interfaces, and quarterly source-code dependency checks.
5) Remediation SLA policy (internal practice to align on contract): Critical: 7 calendar days; High: 30 calendar days; Medium: 90; Low: 180. We document exceptions and freeze releases if critical risk is unresolved.
6) Vulnerability disclosure: Redwood prefers coordinated disclosure with a 45-day default window. If MedSys requires a different timeline we can document it in the MAA.
7) Pen/assessments: we can share redacted external assessment reports (attacker-facing findings) under NDA. For on-prem / customer-hosted deployments, we provide a scan-playbook and support your team during assessment windows.

I've attached a sample Redwood-Auth-Scan-Playbook.pdf and a redaction checklist to speed review. If you can add the procurement contact we will route an NDA (DocuSign) and then provide the full assessment artifacts.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
